import pytest
from isort.parse import skip_line

def test_skip_line():
    # Test cases for skip_line function
    test_cases = [
        # Basic line without quotes or semicolons
        (["This is a line without quotes", "", 0, [], True], (False, "")),
        
        # Line with a string in single quotes
        (["print('Hello World')", "", 0, [], True], (False, "")),
        
        # Line with a string in double quotes
        (['print("Hello World")', "", 0, [], True], (False, "")),
        
        # Line with a semicolon and needs import
        (["Some code; some other code", "", 0, [], True], (True, "")),
        
        # Line with an import statement, should not skip
        (["import os", "", 0, [], True], (False, "")),
        
        # Line that is a comment only
        (["# This is a comment", "", 0, [], True], (False, "")),
        
        # Line with a triple double quote
        (['"""This is a docstring"""', "", 0, [], True], (True, '"""')),
        
        # Line with a triple single quote
        (["'''This is a docstring'''", "", 0, [], True], (True, "'''")),
        
        # Line with an escaped single quote
        (["escaped quote: \\'", "", 0, [], True], (False, ""))
    ]
    
    for i, (input_data, expected) in enumerate(test_cases):
        result = skip_line(*input_data)
        assert result == expected, f'Test case {i} failed: expected {expected}, got {result}'
